blocks.text: Research is rarely a linear process. You start with a question, open a database, find a case, and then get interrupted by a message or a phone call. Each time you switch your attention, your brain takes 23 minutes to fully regain focus on the task. This is the hidden cost of a fragmented workflow.

Information overload happens because you are likely juggling multiple browser tabs for different matters. When you have a tab for a Westlaw search, another for a client document, and a third for an internal email, you invite confusion. Cross-matter contamination is not just a risk to your efficiency, it is an ethical risk to your firm.

The financial impact is clear. If you spend extra time navigating between platforms, you are effectively reducing your billable output. Beyond the money, there is the human cost. Burnout is common when you spend your day fighting your tools rather than doing the actual work. Over 70% of legal errors are linked back to research, which means that speed is not just about profit, it is about accuracy.

items: Use a workspace manager like SupaSidebar to isolate tabs by matter. This keeps your research contained and prevents you from accidentally looking at the wrong case files.
Master your browser's keyboard shortcuts. Use ⌘ + T to open a new tab and ⌃ + ⇥ to cycle through your open tabs without reaching for your mouse.
Create a standard folder structure on your Mac for every new matter. Do not rely on your downloads folder to organize your research PDFs.
Use PDF Expert to annotate your research directly. It is faster than printing documents and scanning them back into your system.

blocks.text: Lazur acts as a bridge between your different apps. Because it lives in the notch of your Mac, you can hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask a question without moving your hands from the keyboard. If you need to find a specific setting in a complex legal database, ask Lazur to point it out. It will draw a circle on your screen to show you exactly where to click.
